subject: Subprocessor certification & cross-border transfer playbook
messages:
From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@globalbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@globalbank.com>
Date: 2025-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: certification and transfer playbook for onboarding

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking our call this morning. As part of GlobalBank's vendor onboarding check we need: 1) a certified list of current subprocessors (including locations and encryption controls), 2) a short playbook describing how you handle cross-border transfers and the fallback when a jurisdiction has restriction, and 3) a one-page summary of how Redwood supports DPIA/art28/art30 evidence for processors.

Our audit team would like to receive the artifacts and an estimate for an on-site or remote evidence review by next week (week of Oct 6). Are any of your subprocessors under an escrow arrangement or otherwise third-party certified? Also please confirm retention and export controls for EU production data.

Appreciate a short timeline and any pre-packaged evidence you can share.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Miller
Vendor Risk Manager, GlobalBank
[sara.miller@globalbank.com]

[Attachment: onboarding-checklist-GLOBALBANK.pdf]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Miller <sara.miller@globalbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: certification and transfer playbook for onboarding

Sara — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support. Quick answers up front:

- We attached a current subprocessor manifest (Redwood_Subprocessor_List_v2.xlsx) with regions and primary security controls.
- We do not currently hold an escrow arrangement for model weights or data; we do have customer-configurable export controls and EU-region processing options.
- ART28/30 ledger (summary) and a one-page DPIA extract are attached (ART28_30_Ledger.pdf, DPIA-summary.docx).

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik to confirm any subprocessor changes in the last 30 days and call out vendors with cross-border flows.
2) Laura to propose an evidence review format (remote first; on-site if required).
3) I will provide a short playbook that maps request flows -> transfer legal basis -> fallback routing to EU-only model variants by EOD Friday (Oct 2).

If your audit team has a template or specific questions, please send them; we'll slot those into the pack.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Privacy & Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Subprocessor_List_v2.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Sara Miller <sara.miller@globalbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-29T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: certification and transfer playbook for onboarding

Sara / Mina — I reviewed the manifest. A couple of technical clarifications for GlobalBank:

- Of the listed subprocessors, two (edge-cache provider A and telemetry vendor B) have occasional cross-border telemetry to the US for analytics; those flows are pseudonymized and encrypted in transit with TLS 1.3.
- EU production is logically segmented; we support customer-managed KMS for keys used to encrypt persistent stores in EU regions.
- For fallback: when a requested model family cannot be served from the EU region (capacity exhausted), routing policy falls back to compatible quantized variants that meet EU data residency policy, and we log any such fallback in the ART28_30_Ledger.

I also attached a short note describing our retention enforcement (retention-policy-snippet.txt) and a checklist we use for evidence reviews. Happy to jump on a 30-min tech walkthrough with your audit engineers — propose Oct 7 or Oct 8.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retention-policy-snippet.txt]

From: Procurement Team <procurement@globalbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Miller <sara.miller@globalbank.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-01T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: certification and transfer playbook for onboarding

Mina — thanks for the materials. A few procurement items before we schedule the audit: please confirm whether Redwood will accept a limited DPA amendment that adds an express audit right clause for our EU accounts (we can provide proposed language). Also confirm availability windows for remote evidence review (Oct 6–10 preferred). Lastly, any customer-specific subprocessor list that can be exported per-account (so we can tie to our contract) would be helpful.

—Procurement Team
GlobalBank

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@globalbank.com>, Sara Miller <sara.miller@globalbank.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-02T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: certification and transfer playbook for onboarding

Hi Procurement / Sara — appreciate the callouts. For clarity:

- Redwood can agree to a narrow, contract-annotated audit right limited to EU production accounts and the scope you define (no unfettered access). We prefer a remote evidence review as the default; if on-site is ultimately needed we will scope and quote that separately.
- We will prepare a customer-scoped subprocessor export (per-account CSV) and provide it via secure link before the remote review.
- Mina will deliver the playbook and a short executive summary by EOD Oct 2 (attached). Marissa will coordinate the audit schedule and the technical walkthrough with Karthik.

Action items:
- Mina: final playbook + executive summary (EOD Oct 2)
- Marissa: propose remote slots Oct 7–9 and confirm attendee list
- Karthik: be available for a 30-min technical walkthrough Oct 7 or 8

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Business Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: executive-summary-onboarding-playbook.pdf]
